script.base: Baltimore is a 3-point favorite with a 21.2 implied total and Lamar Jackson out, so Tyler Huntley starts a low-event game (total 39.5), not a shootout. Base flow is run-leaning but not run-exclusive: Derrick Henry (73 carries, 264 yards over weeks 3-5) is the closer against a Cleveland defense allowing 4.70 YPC, while Huntley is still asked for roughly high-20s to low-30s passes in a one-score game. Cleveland with Deshaun Watson (Dillon Gabriel out) has been inefficient (0.04 EPA/db vs blitz, 0.06 vs none) and is implied for only 18.2, so they hang around without pushing pace.
script.flip1: Huntley turns it over or Cleveland scores first, Baltimore trails by 10+, Henry's clock-killing carries stall, and targets bunch to Zay Flowers, Mark Andrews and Rashod Bateman while Denzel Boston and Harold Fannin get the trailing-script bump.
script.flip2: Cleveland's offense stalls, Baltimore leads by two scores late, Henry and Justice Hill grind the clock, and Watson dropbacks plus Boston's deep shots dry up. A true blowout is the lesser branch at only a field-goal spread, so starter snap risk is a possible fourth-quarter trim, not a benching.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and Bateman under 19.5 lost the over. Jackson's absence was the whole story: Huntley threw about 24 times, Flowers and Andrews took the checkdowns, and Bateman, the 10.5-aDOT piece, saw two looks for under 15 yards. The last four lines of 88, 37, 46 and 62 were Jackson games, and the move to a 19.5 coin-flip was the market already pricing that, not a stale number. Cleveland did not need a shutdown corner; a backup quarterback and a 21-point team total were enough. That counter is close to as strong as the read, which is why this stays a lean flag and not a strong ticket. Henry over would have lost the same Monday if the center-less line got him to 75 yards on 22 carries against a bad front, which is why 90.5 was passed rather than flagged as strong.
slip_story: No bet placed. The only live lean is a low-bar Baltimore pass-game piece (Bateman over 19.5) inside a competitive 39.5 script, and it should not be parlayed with a total under or with Henry under. The run-stack (Henry over, Hill change-of-pace) was the base story but the 90.5 rung failed, so there is no run slip. Flowers would have been the correlated pass partner and was passed on price after the Huntley haircut. Do not add Boston, Fannin or Watson overs; they need the opposite, higher-event Cleveland script. No third leg, no TDs, one market per player.
